turns.t: Hi. Sorry, I'm a few minutes late, the lot out front was full.
Oh, don't worry, that lot is a nightmare on Thursdays. And this rain, it was sunny an hour ago. Did you end up parking on the street?
Garage across the road. Eleven dollars.
Ouch. Well, you're here now. Your chart says it's your diabetes check, the sugars have been creeping up. Is that how you see it?
Yeah. The numbers on my meter are higher lately.
How high are we talking, roughly? What do you see in the morning?
Around one-sixty. Used to be one-ten.
Okay, that's a real change. Have you noticed anything in yourself, anything that feels different?
I'm thirsty a lot. More than normal.
Thirstier than normal. How long has that been going on?
About one month.
And what about the bathroom, are you going more often?
Up at night to pee. Twice, sometimes three times.
Twice or three times a night. Is that new as well, or have you always been a night-time person?
New. I used to sleep straight through.
Got it. Any blurry vision, like you can't quite focus on the page?
No. Eyes are fine.
Good. Remind me, when were you diagnosed with the type 2 diabetes?
Three years ago. And high cholesterol, same time.
Right, type 2 diabetes for three years, plus the high cholesterol. And you're managing with diet alone, no pills so far?
Right. Just diet. The walks stopped when it got cold, though.
Tell me about the diet. I'm always curious what people actually eat, not what they think they should say.
Lots of rice. Bread. My wife makes banana bread on Sundays.
Banana bread, I love banana bread, I won't hold that against you. Do you smoke at all?
Never smoked.
And alcohol, do you drink?
A couple of beers on the weekend.
That's moderate. Okay, let me check a few numbers. I'll take your blood pressure, then we'll put you on the scale.
Blood pressure comes out at 134 over 82. A touch high, but I'd want it again before I worry. Step up here for me, please.
Okay.
Weight is 94 kilograms. Last year you were 90, so a few kilos have crept on over the winter. Now, take your sock off, I want to look at your feet.
Which one?
Left first. I'm touching a few spots with this thin little thread, tell me when you feel it.
Yep. Yep. Yeah, I feel that.
Good, sensation in both feet is normal. And the pulses at the ankles are strong, so the circulation looks fine.
That's good, right?
Very good. So here's my thinking. It looks like your blood sugar control is slipping, mostly from the winter routine, the extra rice and bread, and the walks stopping.
So I need pills?
Not yet. Let's get an accurate picture first. I'd like to order an HbA1c, which tells us the average of the last three months. We'll draw it today at the lab downstairs.
Okay. Is that all?
I'd also like a urine test for protein, since diabetes can affect the kidneys over the years. You can give that sample on your way out.
Fine.
In the meantime, go back to walking, even twenty minutes after dinner, and try swapping half the rice for vegetables. Banana bread, one slice, not three.
My wife won't like that.
Tell her it's doctor's orders. Let's meet again in two weeks, when the results are back, and talk about whether medicine makes sense.
Two weeks. Okay.
Great. Take care of yourself, and if the rain stops, maybe skip the garage next time.
Ha. Thanks, doc.
